body:
Founder asked to regenerate the extension 1000 PJSIP password and store it in EMILY/var, since sudo-queue/52's original generation was deliberately never printed anywhere retrievable. Cannot execute this myself -- no passwordless sudo, not in the asterisk group, can't read /etc/asterisk/* or connect to the Asterisk control socket (all confirmed directly this session). Wrote sudo-queue/53-regenerate-carepyre-phone-password.sh following this repo's own established pattern: generates a fresh secret (openssl rand -hex 16, same method as the original), writes it to EMILY/var/carepyre-phone-secret.env (mode 600) this time so it's actually retrievable, substitutes it into the live /etc/asterisk/pjsip_carepyre_phone.conf, and reloads PJSIP. Queued for the founder to run with real sudo. Session: sess-20260905-0712-8908a299

⚓ ☃
title: CAREPYRE-42143124 follow-up: queued SIP phone password regeneration (sudo-queue/53)
